source_snapshot.procedure: Send `ipmitool sensor list | grep -i power` and check the power-consumption data.
source_snapshot.criteria: Power-consumption data is readable and correct, and the data is the same as in BMC WebUI.
source_snapshot.deepseek: YES adds a guessed `/redfish/v1/Chassis/1/Power` endpoint, `curl -k`, command-line credentials and raw user comparison without proving which reading is CPU power or aligning units/sample windows.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION correctly requires exact CPU sensor/WebUI mapping, protected access, units, freshness, synchronized capture and an approved comparison tolerance.

old_problem: Generic `grep power` can select chassis, PSU, cap or CPU sensors and does not establish correctness. IPMI explains how sensor values and units are derived from the SDR, while Redfish provides discoverable Sensor readings and data-source links; however, neither standard assigns an OEM sensor name to this Project's CPU or defines equality across independently sampled WebUI values. Those exact mappings and tolerance are bounded versioned Project inputs.
disposition_reason: Preserve the original IPMI sensor-list/grep checkpoint for coverage but qualify its output against a Project-approved CPU-specific SDR sensor mapping. Capture value, unit, status, identity and timestamp, then compare it to the same metric in the actual BMC WebUI during a synchronized window using a preapproved tolerance that accounts for resolution and averaging. A discovered Redfish Sensor may corroborate the mapping but cannot replace either the IPMI command or visual WebUI evidence.
decision_basis: XLSX row 987, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, tests JSON, selection manifest, historical V3.1 record and physical rows 988-989 were directly reviewed; row 988 is baseline-completed, so next pending was verified as Functionality row 989 / variant c81071b0cf544979.

IPMI v2.0 specifies that management software converts raw analog sensor readings using SDR conversion factors and vendor-selected units. Therefore the SDR identity, conversion/unit and sensor status—not a text grep alone—are required evidence.

DMTF Redfish Sensor resources expose a Reading and ReadingUnits with DataSourceUri linkage, but resource discovery and semantic mapping are required; `/Chassis/1/Power` and aggregate PowerControl cannot be assumed to be CPU power.

The source explicitly requires BMC WebUI equality. ED-08 preserves an actual rendered WebUI capture; asynchronous sources need a Project-approved sampling window and numeric tolerance. Without an approved tolerance no PASS is allowed under ED-15.

ED-03, ED-08, ED-13, ED-15, ED-17, ED-19, ED-21 and ED-30 preserve standard/OEM separation, visual evidence, N/A proof, objective acceptance and per-case identity; ED-33, ED-34, ED-36 and ED-38 permit parameterized protected read-only collection without log clearing.

test_case.test_name: Read the mapped CPU current-power sensor and compare with synchronized BMC WebUI
test_case.purpose: Verify that the exact BMC exposes a readable, healthy CPU current-power metric through the source IPMI sensor path and that its normalized value agrees with the same rendered WebUI metric within an approved synchronized tolerance, without confusing CPU power with chassis, PSU or cap data.
required_package: Immutable SUT/BMC/firmware/WebUI identity and vendor/Project-approved mapping from CPU/package/socket scope to exact IPMI SDR record/sensor number/name and WebUI field
Pinned ipmitool/SDR parser and reviewed Script revision; SDR conversion, unit, resolution, accuracy/status and unavailable/stale rules
Approved WebUI route/widget and actual rendered capture method with authenticated, certificate-verified, secret-safe access
Versioned definition of instantaneous versus averaged value, UI refresh cadence, synchronized sampling window and numeric comparison tolerance
Optional discovered Redfish Sensor URI/property with Reading, ReadingUnits and data-source mapping; no hard-coded `/Chassis/1/Power` assumption
Stable workload/power observation condition, clock synchronization, evidence redaction and no-mutation audit
test_case.test_command: READ-ONLY HYBRID PROCEDURE ONLY; DO NOT RUN DURING REVIEW. Verify exact SUT/BMC/firmware identity and the approved CPU sensor-to-WebUI map. Preserve logs and capture the complete `ipmitool sensor list` output through protected access, retaining the source `grep -i power` result as an artifact but selecting only the mapped CPU SDR record. Record sensor number/name, CPU/socket scope, converted value, watts unit, status, raw value/SDR identity where available and timestamp. In the same approved sample window, open the actual BMC WebUI CPU-power field, wait for the documented refresh and capture the rendered page with target/metric/value/unit/time context. Optionally read the discovered certificate-verified Redfish Sensor as corroboration. Normalize only approved units/averaging, compare IPMI and WebUI within the approved tolerance, and emit PASS/FAIL/NOT READY. Do not clear logs, change caps, stress CPUs or alter power.
test_case.expected_result: The mapped CPU current-power IPMI sensor is present, healthy, fresh and readable in watts with valid SDR conversion, and the actual WebUI renders the same CPU scope/metric. Values captured in the approved synchronized window agree within the approved tolerance and sampling model; any supplemental Redfish reading has a documented data-source relationship. No power, cap, workload or log state changes.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires exact BMC/SUT identity, approved CPU-specific sensor/UI mapping, valid SDR conversion/unit/status, fresh timestamped IPMI data, actual rendered WebUI evidence for the same scope and agreement within the preapproved numeric tolerance. A grep hit, unrelated chassis/PSU/cap sensor, exact-equality assumption, guessed Redfish URI, API-only evidence, `curl -k`, empty/NA/stale values or user eyeballing without tolerance cannot pass. Missing mapping/tolerance/capture is NOT READY; N/A is allowed only when approved platform specification proves CPU-specific telemetry is unsupported.
safety_gate: Read only. Deny power-cap writes, stress launch, throttle changes, resets, power transitions and log clearing.
Use certificate/endpoint verification and secret-safe credentials; do not use `curl -k` or passwords in arguments/evidence.
Require an approved CPU sensor mapping before selecting any grep result; stop on duplicate, ambiguous, aggregate or unknown-scope readings.
Require declared units, sampling/averaging semantics, synchronized window and tolerance before comparison; no threshold means no PASS.
Preserve actual rendered WebUI evidence and raw IPMI evidence. Supplemental Redfish cannot silently replace either source checkpoint.
Stop on invalid SDR conversion, non-OK sensor status, stale/unavailable value, wrong target or mismatch beyond tolerance; do not change the DUT to make readings agree.
expected_evidence: SUT/BMC/firmware/WebUI identity and approved CPU/socket-to-IPMI-SDR-to-WebUI mapping
Complete redacted IPMI sensor-list artifact plus mapped sensor number/name/raw and converted value/unit/status/timestamp/SDR revision
Actual rendered WebUI capture showing the same CPU scope, value, unit and synchronized observation context
Sampling/averaging model, clocks, approved tolerance and normalized comparison calculation
Optional discovered Redfish Sensor/Reading/ReadingUnits/DataSourceUri evidence, no-mutation audit and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: No mutation is expected. On access, mapping, freshness or comparison failure, close read-only sessions, preserve evidence and correct only the Project sensor/UI map, certificate/access configuration or sampling model under owner control. Do not clear logs, change a cap, alter workload or power-cycle to force agreement.

source_conflict.reason: Procedure and Criteria coherently require an IPMI CPU-power read plus WebUI comparison. The missing OEM sensor mapping and tolerance are Project bindings, not competing requirements.

blocked.reason: Standards define sensor conversion and discoverable telemetry structure. The exact OEM CPU sensor/UI mapping, cadence and tolerance are finite versioned Project prerequisites.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: CPU/socket-to-IPMI SDR and WebUI mapping; firmware/UI build; units/conversion/status; sampling window/averaging/tolerance; protected access; optional discovered Redfish mapping and evidence route.
pending.execution_status: NOT STARTED; REVIEW-LAYER READ-ONLY HYBRID CASE ONLY; NO IPMI, REDFISH, WEBUI, LOG, POWER, CAP, STRESS OR DUT ACTION EXECUTED

external_authorities.title: Intelligent Platform Management Interface Specification v2.0 rev. 1.1
external_authorities.application: Section 36.5 explains that management software uses SDR conversion factors to turn raw sensor readings into vendor-selected units; identity, conversion and units are required for a correct reading.

external_authorities.title: DMTF Redfish Resource and Schema Guide 2025.3
external_authorities.application: Defines Sensor Reading/ReadingUnits and DataSourceUri relationships used for discovered supplemental telemetry; it does not make a guessed chassis aggregate CPU-specific.

external_authorities.title: DMTF Redfish Data Model Specification 2025.3
external_authorities.application: Provides schema discovery and resource-model rules supporting service-root traversal instead of a hard-coded `/Chassis/1/Power` URI.

project_authority: The Project/vendor owner binds the exact CPU sensor, socket scope and WebUI field, defines sampling/averaging and tolerance, and proves N/A when telemetry is unsupported. These versioned values are runtime configuration and do not leave the review method undecidable.
